description: _cte_reference_ids decides CTE exclusion by source name: sqlglot's _traverse_tables overwrites a name-keyed sources entry when an unqualified CTE reference or derived table follows a same-named/aliased base table, so the base exp.Table is excluded and a SQLite catalog read (e.g. WITH sqlite_master AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM main.sqlite_master, sqlite_master; WITH c AS (SELECT 1 AS k) SELECT * FROM sqlite_master AS c, c; SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master, (SELECT 1 AS k) AS sqlite_master) is classified as a data query. Makes the diff-added docstring (readonly.py 140-143, 'never by name ... sqlglot renames the base-table source key') and docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:75 untrue. No test covers the collision.

RunSqlTool's dialect must match its runner's hard-coded dialect, but only a docstring enforces it; dialect defaults to None and is a public writable attribute, and SqlRunner does not expose its dialect. A programmatic caller omitting dialect over a MySQL runner gets '# c\nSELECT ...' reported as 'row(s) affected' with rows dropped.

When RunSqlTool's dialect disagrees with the runner's, the tool returns success=True 'N row(s) affected' and silently drops result rows; no guard, log or error. Shipped server unaffected (build_agent passes URL dialect); programmatic callers affected.

Diff-added TestGuardDoesNotCrashOnPinnedSqlglot docstring (and read-only-safety.md:240) says the deny-walk's exp.Alter entry still rejects ALTER, but test_nested_alter_still_rejected sends a root-level ALTER rejected by the root-type gate (readonly.py:590) before the deny-walk (line 599); the test passes with exp.Alter removed from _DML_DDL_TYPES.

first_sql_keyword dialect resolution: an unknown dialect silently becomes the generic tokenizer with no log (sibling is_introspection_query logs WARNING); Dialect.get(None/unknown) also scans entry_points and attempts an import on every call.
first_sql_keyword's '' covers no token, non-word first token and TokenError; it also returns any unquoted identifier while called a keyword.
first_sql_keyword docstring says '#' opens a comment only for mysql; BigQuery and ClickHouse tokenizers also treat '#' as a comment. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.

Garbled pyproject comment about first_sql_keyword vs _mysql_parse_sql disagreement; _cte_reference_ids docstring omits in-place normalization and its log names scope analysis when normalization raised. Behavior-inert prose cap applied.
Scope-analysis fallback log records only the exception type at INFO; matches criterion, missing context.
Empty-SQL check uses str.strip(), so comment-only SQL reaches the runner and with read_only off is reported as a green '1 row(s) affected'. Pre-existing.
first_sql_keyword and is_read_shaped tokenize the same SQL twice (same in is_introspection_query).
